routes.label: Model the fourth tank with an equation
Make all four tanks match the fourth

question:
Rohan keeps a total of \(90\) guppies in \(4\) fish tanks.

• There is \(1\) more guppy in the \(2\)nd tank than in the \(1\)st tank.

• There are \(2\) more guppies in the \(3\)rd tank than in the \(2\)nd tank.

• There are \(3\) more guppies in the \(4\)th tank than in the \(3\)rd tank.

How many guppies are in the \(4\)th tank?
solution:
The fourth tank has \(3\) more guppies than the third, \(3+2=5\) more than the second, and \(3+2+1=6\) more than the first.

Imagine adding \(6\), \(5\), and \(3\) guppies to the first, second, and third tanks, respectively. All four tanks would then have as many guppies as the fourth tank. Their new total would be
\[
90+6+5+3=104.
\]
These four equal groups each contain \(104\div4=26\) guppies. The original tank counts are therefore \(20,21,23,26\), which have the stated differences and sum to \(90\). Thus the fourth tank contains \(\boxed{26}\) guppies, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
